full_judgment:
12. Next comes the second face of the case. Respondent No.4 Alhaj Oil Mills Limited, Head Office filed Other Suit No.214 of 2003 in the Court of Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Chittagong claiming the ownership of the 3,000 MT of Crude Palm Olein in question. In that case seller Walmar Trading Pte Ltd. as defendant No.1 filed an application under Order 7 rule 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure for rejection of the plaint of Other Suit No.214 of 2003 which was allowed and the plaint of the case was rejected by judgment and decree dated 1-3-2004 and against the said judgment and decree respondent No.4 filed First Appeal No.70 of 2004 before this Division which was also dismissed by judgment and order dated 26-10-2005 affirming the judgment and decree dated 1-3-2004 by the Joint District Judge, Chittagong and against the said judgment and order of the First Appeal No.70 of 2004 respondent No.4 filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No.264 of 2006 dated 23-10-2005 and leave was granted for which respondent No.4 filed Civil Appeal No. 99 of 2006 which was dismissed on 21-7-2009 by the Appellate Division and thereafter respondent No.4 filed Civil Review No.103 of 2009 for reviewing the judgment and order dated 22-7-2009 which was also dismissed by the Appellate Division as being not pressed by the respondent No. 4. 

 14. Mr Hasan Md Reyad, the learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioner after taking us with the petition and different. Annexures with it mainly submits that since the plaint of the respondent No.4 claiming ownership of the consignment in question was rejected by the judgment and decree in Other Suit No.214 of 2003 which was upheld up to the Appellate Division, there is no bar to release the consignment in question in favour of the petitioner but the respondent No.1 Commissioner of Customs, Chittagong despite receiving of the order of the Appellate Division withheld the release of the petitioner's goods without any justification and, as such, the said withholding of goods is liable to be declared to have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. In elaborating his submission the learned counsel took us to the pertinent portion of the judgment passed by the High Court Division in writ petition No.7428 of 2003 wherein this Division gave a clear direction upon the Customs authority in the manner, "We also direct Customs Authority not to deal with the goods in question in either way till the decision of the civil Court."  Therefore, the learned counsel for the petitioner contends that the dispute regarding the ownership of the goods in question since reached its finality up to the Appellate Division of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh, Customs Authority has no legal bar to release the goods in favour of the petitioner-company.
